blogs.title: The Missing Genital Ulcer: Serial Exams and the Bedside Diagnosis of Behçet’s
blogs.description: This post would focus on how Behçet’s disease is often diagnosed clinically rather than radiographically or serologically, and why repeated skin and mucosal examinations matter. Using this case, it would highlight how oral aphthae and folliculitis-like lesions were initially suggestive but the later appearance of a scrotal ulcer made the diagnosis much clearer, underscoring the value of serial reassessment and careful use of the International Criteria for Behçet’s Disease.

blogs.title: Normal MRI, Inflamed CNS: How to Recognize Acute Neuro-Behçet’s Anyway
blogs.description: This post would examine the diagnostic tension created by a patient with headache, vertigo, aseptic meningitis, and a completely unremarkable brain MRI. It would review the non-parenchymal or early-phase presentations of acute neuro-Behçet’s, explain why a normal MRI does not exclude the diagnosis, and discuss how CSF findings plus the systemic Behçet phenotype can justify the diagnosis after infection and malignancy are reasonably excluded.

blogs.title: When Sodium Tells the Story: SIADH as a Clue to Neuroinflammation
blogs.description: This post would use the case to explore SIADH as more than just an electrolyte problem, framing it as a potential marker of CNS inflammation. It would review the classic diagnostic framework for SIADH, discuss how neuroinflammatory states can drive ADH release, and consider the plausible role of cytokine signaling such as IL-6 in linking acute neuro-Behçet’s to hyponatremia.

blogs.title: Hiccups, Rhabdo, and Hyponatremia: The Strange Bedfellows of SIADH
blogs.description: This post would zoom in on the underrecognized clinical consequences of significant hyponatremia, especially persistent hiccups and elevated CK/rhabdomyolysis. It would emphasize that these findings can look unrelated to sodium at first glance, but in neuroinflammatory patients they may be important clues to the severity and systemic impact of SIADH.

blogs.title: Steroids Optional? What to Make of Colchicine-Only Treatment in Acute Neuro-Behçet’s
blogs.description: This post would tackle the therapeutic controversy raised by this case: a patient with acute neuro-Behçet’s improved without corticosteroids or other immunosuppressants. It would compare the usual standard approach to acute neuro-Behçet’s with this apparent colchicine-responsive course, discuss whether this reflects true efficacy versus spontaneous improvement, and outline when a steroid-sparing strategy may or may not be reasonable.

blogs.title: Broad Differential, Narrow Thinking: Diagnostic Stewardship in Fever, Headache, and Aseptic Meningitis
blogs.description: This post would analyze the early workup strategy in a patient who looked infectious, inflammatory, and potentially malignant all at once. It would discuss the appropriate role of empiric cefepime and acyclovir, the limits of shotgun testing such as ACE or sIL-2R in low-pretest-probability settings, and how clinicians can stay appropriately broad without overvaluing nonspecific results.
